TS: Identification of loading tackle used (sheets, ropes, chains, etc.), as specified in DCU 9 to CIM Article 13; and of containers, as specified in Articles 5 and 10 of Annex III to CIM (CIM 17).
MPA: A panel which can be moved.
IL: Lidded stackable rigid tray compliant with CEN TS 14482:2002.
PL: A piece of equipment normally having a flat surface, or prepared for carrying cargo with a specific shape.
PBP: A box pallet identified as being privately owned.
FPN: A flat euro-pallet that may not be exchanged.
FPR: A non-exchangeable flat pallet owned by a railroad.
TSU: A device to support a tarpaulin.
BB: Cargoes in bulk not stuffed in equipment.
LU: A mechanical device used in the loading and/or unloading of cargo into and from transport equipment.
BL: A piece of equipment that is normally a piece of wood to fix cargo (e.g. coils) during transport.
BR: Flat bottomed inland cargo vessel for canals and rivers with or without own propulsion for the purpose of transported goods. (Synonym: Lighter).
TE: A vehicle without motive power, designed for the carriage of cargo and to be towed by a motor vehicle.
EFP: A flat euro-pallet that may be exchanged.
EFQ: Standard pallet with dimensions 40 X 30 cm.
EFU: Pallet need not be returned to the point of expedition.
EFV: Pallet must be returned to the point of expedition.
EFW: A container for the storage or movement of bottles, a.k.a. bottlerack.
EFX: A non-protected cylindrical container with a narrow neck made usually of glass or plastic which is especially used for liquids.
TP: Waterproof material, e.g. canvas, to spread over cargo to protect it from getting wet.
DPA: A set of panels fixed inside a porthole.
DPC: A fixed gantry crane ashore for container handling operations.
DPD: A mobile crane for handling operations.
DPE: A crane mounted on a dedicated vessel.
DPF: A crane mounted on a ship for handling operations.
DPH: Equipment device for handling and moving goods.
DPJ: Equipment device at the rear of a truck for loading and unloading cargo.
DPK: Standard pallet with dimensions 80 X 60 cm.
DPL: Equipment permanently on board a means of transport.
DPM: Standard pallet with dimensions 80 X 120 cm.
DPN: Standard pallet with dimensions 100 X 120 cm.
DPO: Standard pallet with dimensions 60 X 40 cm.
EYP: A euro-pallet of type Y that may be exchanged.
SW: Rectangular equipment unit without wheels, which can be mounted on a chassis or positioned on legs.
AB: Chain used in the securing of cargo.
RG: A generator used to control the temperature in temperature-controlled transport equipment.
RF: A railway wagon without raised sides or ends.
RO: Rope used in the securing of cargo.
RR: To identify that the equipment is a rail car.
BPO: A road vehicle capable of carrying goods which is being carried on another means of transport.
CH: A wheeled carriage onto which an ocean container is mounted for inland conveyance.
EFY: A lidded package which can be made of cardboard, wood, plastic,tin,etc.
CN: Equipment item as defined by ISO for transport. It must be of: A) permanent character, strong enough for repeated use; B) designed to facilitate the carriage of goods, by one or more modes of transport, without intermediate reloading; C) fitted with devices for its ready handling, particularly.
PFP: A flat pallet identified as being privately owned.
EFZ: A box mounted on a pallet base under the control of CHEP.
EGA: A package such as a box.
EGB: A package used for the dispaly of goods, usually during a promotion.
EGC: A case used for products which require constant temperature control.
EGD: Collars, with the dimensions 80cms * 100cms, which when fitted onto a pallet enable the pallet to be transformed into a box pallet with, if necessary, a lid.
EGE: Collars, with the dimensions 80cms * 120cms, which when fitted onto a pallet enable the pallet to be transformed into a box pallet with, if necessary, a lid.
EGF: A flat receptacle with low sides for carrying or holding articles.
EGG: A three sided cage mounted on wheels.
EGH: A low cart for the transportation and storage of groceries, milk, etc.
EGI: A generator located landside at a terminal, used to provide electric power to a vessel or other means of transport.
RGF: Storage tank or facility capable of receiving shipment of goods or commodity.
BPN: A box pallet which cannot be exchanged.
STR: A narrow strip of flexible material.
BPP: A road vehicle capable of carrying goods with an attached trailer which is being carried on another means of transport.
BPQ: A trailer accompanied by a self-propelling tractor unit which is being carried on another means of transport.
BPR: Bag intended primarily for the conveyance of postal items.
BPU: Tray intended primarily for the conveyance of letter mail items of from C5 up to in excess of C4, in which the items are stacked one on top of another. May also be used for letter mail smaller items stood on their long edge.
BPV: Postal item which is conveyed individually, with only the wrapping provided by the mailer for protection.
BPW: Device, consisting of a flat surface mounted on a wheels, which is designed for the conveyance of items which may safely be stacked. Normally also equipped with a handle to allow the device to be easily manoeuvred.
BPX: The container is not compliant with the Customs Convention on Containers.
BPY: A euro-pallet of type Y that may not be exchanged.
AA: Ground equipment being fuelled or serviced.
PA: A platform on which goods can be stacked in order to facilitate the movement by a forklift or sling.
AD: Temperature recorder to provide a record of the actual temperature.
AE: The part of the vehicle where the cargo is loaded.
AG: A cardboard platform used for holding product for storage or transportation.
AH: A code to indicate that there is no special equipment needed.
AI: A compartment forming part of a transport vessel.
AJ: Type of open container used for carrying objects.
AK: To indicate that the equipment is an aircraft.
AL: A device used for medical purposes.
AM: A refrigerated (reefer) container that is actively cooling the product.
AN: A pallet with standard dimensions 80*120 centimetres made of synthetic material.
AO: A standard pallet with standard dimensions 100*120 centimetres made of synthetic material.
AP: Equipment used to store and transport clothing in a hanging position.
AQ: Trailer designated for combined road/rail use.
AT: Empty rail wagon added to the loaded wagons, when goods are longer than the loaded wagon.
BPS: Tray intended primarily for the conveyance of letter mail items of size slightly exceeding C5, in which the items are stood on their long edge.
